title: Very high LA on server after update to v1.14.0
body:
I updated my test server from v1.13.6 to v1.14.0
I got high Server LA

My use case is
1. search input vectors (batching) (~ 100 - 1000 queries with limit 1)
2. process search results
3. update vectors with blocking API (~ 100 - 2000 points)

## Current Behavior
It picture is  from monitoring.
1 section - qdrant v1.13.6. from: 6:00 to: 11:30
2. section - qdrant v1.14.0. from: 11:30 to: 16:50
3. section - revert qdrant v1.13.6

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5935f221-ae27-4234-ace2-bb57b70caeeb)

## Context (Environment)
server has 56 CPUs

I tried
1. set `incremental_hnsw_building: false` in config
2. change value for collection `optimizer_config.max_optimization_threads`. `null -> 2`
3. change value for collection `hnsw_config.max_indexing_threads`. `0` -> `8`
4. change value in config file `performance.update_rate_limit`. `null` -> `32`
5. change value in config file `service.max_workers`. `0` -> `32`

It did not work.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Could you share the following?
1. collection configuration (`GET /collections/name`)
2. collection distribution (if you have multiple peers) (`GET /collections/name/cluster`)
3. an example of one of your search requests
4. how many batches are you sending concurrently, just one or multiple?
5. what is QPS like in 1.13.6 and in 1.14.0?

Could you try the following:
1. is using much smaller batches (10 queries) faster?

It could potentially be related to <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/6326>.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I faced the same issue. My nodes were restarted around 3 AM(maybe because of node pool auto-upgrade), and that’s when the Qdrant pods got updated from v1.13.6 to v1.14.0 — I didn’t trigger any upgrade myself. Right after that, I noticed a sharp spike in both CPU and memory usage. This happened even though I never explicitly upgraded via Helm. The only event was a node restart in the cluster. Here’s the usage pattern from my GKE dashboard — there’s a clear jump on April 24th: Separately, I realized my Helm config had the image tag left empty: ``` image: repository: docker.io/qdrant/qdrant tag: "" ``` Since the tag was "", Kubernetes pulled the latest image during pod recreation, which explains how the version changed even though I never explicitly upgraded it. This silent upgrade caught me off guard. Happy to share additional logs or metrics if it would help troubleshoot further.
